A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FS-Merge research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLP, vision-transformer and BERT merging experiments, including accuracy measurements, data-size studies and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds corruption tests, alternative pretraining settings, larger-dataset evaluations and eight-model merging results.

M1.justification: The merge/unmerge matrices, frozen source weights, reconstruction objectives, folding procedure and diagonal-plus-low-rank parameterization are retained. Sequential FS-Merge already appears in v1. The added evaluations use existing method variants.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR100-C corruption evaluation and merging across SUN397, Food101 and CIFAR100 (Tables 5 and 27), substantially extending input conditions and scene/food task coverage. The earlier MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, vision-classification and GLUE tasks remain; BERT coverage is not newly introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 add LoRA-based knowledge distillation at several ranks, providing a substantial parameter-efficient comparator to FS-Merge alongside full-model distillation. Existing MLP and BERT comparator sets remain in the appendices. Git Re-Basin is newly analyzed theoretically, not newly evaluated as an empirical baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces heterogeneous-pretraining, shared-initialization, five-severity corruption and eight-model evaluation protocols. The shared-initialization experiment uses average initialization. For the retained main four-model comparison, FS-Merge's reported rank changes from 32 to 24. The new large-dataset augmentation budget is inconsistent: Appendix F.5 states 100 augmented images per dataset, while Table 27 states 1000.

E4.justification: New analyses examine corruption robustness, dependence on pretraining strategy and shared initialization, and scaling to eight models. The original initialization, augmentation, local-versus-global and inner-feature analyses are retained; v1's Appendix H discussion becomes v2's G.3–G.5.

E5.justification: Table 5 newly reports means and standard deviations across five corruption severities. This measures cross-severity dispersion, not uncertainty across repeated training runs. The existing five-seed MLP experiments and three-seed BERT data-size error bars remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 5 and 24–28 add substantial result blocks, while numerous retained scores change. For example, Table 1's FS-Merge accuracy changes from 84.52 to 85.83, and Table 3's DTD/EuroSAT per-task accuracy changes from 63.18 to 62.64. The BERT Average score for QQP/QNLI is corrected from 563.2 to 56.32. Results with changed ranks cannot establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 2.1 and Appendix H's definitions, expressivity theorem, proposition, separating example and proofs comparing FS-Merge with RegMean and Git Re-Basin under rank assumptions. v1 has no corresponding formal analysis. One new proof step needs correction: the displayed M in Eq. 26 has rank d, contrary to the following rank-at-most-r assertion when r is smaller than d.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add superior MLP expressivity as an explicit theoretical contribution and extend the performance claim to distribution shifts. The claim of reproducing arbitrary target MLPs under rank conditions is substantially more specific than v1's informal statements about greater generality.

C2.justification: Appendix F.4 newly qualifies FS-Merge's advantage when models share initialization, noting that cheaper RegMean can perform similarly. F.6 identifies memory limitations preventing full FS-Merge evaluation on eight models. Existing core limitations remain. The new blanket robustness interpretation overstates Table 5: distillation has higher mean accuracy for Gaussian and shot noise in the CIFAR100/EuroSAT comparison.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that BERT classification heads are trainable and documents model provenance, configurations and runtimes for added experiments. Tables 3–4 replace exact optimized-parameter counts with yes/no indicators. The code URL remains, but the footnote no longer states that models are available. Most original implementation details and hyperparameter grids are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds an adapter/parameter-efficient-fine-tuning discussion and distinguishes FS-Merge from Wan et al.'s LLM knowledge fusion. Additional citations support corruption testing, new datasets, feature-rank assumptions and distillation. The established positioning relative to ZipIt, mode connectivity and model merging largely remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial main-text passages are rewritten, and the attention-method explanation is condensed with details referenced in Appendix B. BERT evaluation gains a main-text subsection, the data-size subsection is integrated into vision results, and the conclusion becomes a broader discussion. Appendix discussions are also substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a journal layout, redraws method schematics, expands captions and adds multiple experimental tables. Tables 3–4 gain LoRA rows and revised parameter columns; the main ViT-L table moves to the appendix, and a BERT subset is redisplayed in the main text. The existing data-size plots in Figures 4–7 are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The main gain is substantially stronger empirical support for generality: LoRA-distillation comparisons, corruption tests, varied pretraining, larger tasks and eight-model merging address important gaps in v1's evaluation. The shared-initialization discussion also clarifies when cheaper methods suffice. These gains outweigh localized shortcomings, including Table 27's conflicting augmentation counts, Table 5's overbroad robustness interpretation and the rank error following Eq. 26; the added theory therefore requires correction.
